active_paradigms.idea: Replace repeated feasibility solves with one discretized epigraph MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program first constructs a good greedy solution, performs only single moves and swaps, then runs 11 separate threshold MILPs with a 0.15-second limit each. Its main weakness is that a time-limited HiGHS solve commonly returns a feasible incumbent while result.success is false, so the code discards useful assignments; repeated model construction also spends much of the budget outside branch-and-bound. Build one MILP whose binary variables y[i,g,k] mean model i is placed on GPU g while global pressure level k is selected, together with one-hot level variables z[k]. Use a small grid of pressure bounds spanning the incumbent-derived lower and upper bounds, enforce each model's assignment once, enforce sum_k z[k]=1, and enforce sum_i (weight_i + T_k*size_i)*y[i,g,k] <= 80*T_k*z[k] for every GPU and level. Minimize sum_k T_k*z[k], optionally with a tiny secondary coefficient favoring larger aggregate remaining memory to avoid numerically tight solutions. This is a single MILP call instead of binary-searching many zero-objective feasibility calls, so HiGHS can spend its complete time budget finding and improving an incumbent. A coarse first grid should be enough because the evaluator score is an average across cases; concentrate grid points around the greedy incumbent and the total-load lower bound rather than using uniformly huge ranges. Decode only an integral incumbent and retain the existing greedy placement as fallback.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimizes a discretized global upper bound on maximum KVPR, while eliminating the current repeated-solve/time-limit failure mode and arbitrary zero-objective feasible assignments.
active_paradigms.cautions: This formulation grows as models × GPUs × grid-points, so use perhaps 8–20 levels and skip it for large instances. Do not require solver success before reading a valid integral feasible incumbent if the SciPy result exposes one; independently verify every model appears exactly once and every GPU memory sum is at most 80. Include the original greedy result as an always-valid fallback, and ensure T levels are strictly positive.

active_paradigms.idea: Use exact critical-bin ejection-chain neighborhood search with itertools.combinations
active_paradigms.description: The present local search is trapped whenever improvement requires moving two or more models simultaneously: it considers only one relocation or one pairwise swap and rejects intermediate worsening states. After greedy placement, rank GPUs by current KVPR and select the most pressured GPU plus one or two plausible receiver GPUs. Form the small pool consisting of models on those GPUs, enumerate feasible subsets for the critical GPU with itertools.combinations, and then enumerate or recursively assign the residual pool to the other selected GPUs subject to their memory capacities. Score each complete local repartition by the true maximum KVPR over all GPUs, not by a linear proxy, and apply the best strictly improving repartition. Restrict enumeration to a bounded pool, for example by including all models from a critical GPU and only the most relevant 8–14 models from receiver GPUs, prioritized by high weight, high size, or high weight-per-size impact. Repeat while the global maximum decreases, changing which critical GPU is selected after each accepted repair. This is a large-neighborhood exact repair: unlike the prior successful full subset-partition concept, it is targeted to the bottleneck and therefore remains practical when the whole instance is too large for exact partitioning. It is particularly effective for placements where a large low-weight model must be displaced through a chain before a high-weight model can leave the bottleneck.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The worst GPU's exact KVPR, especially instances where pairwise move/swap local optima are materially worse than a coordinated 3+ model redistribution.
active_paradigms.cautions: Never enumerate all subsets of all models; cap the local pool and preserve models outside the selected GPUs unchanged. Every candidate must check memory before calculating pressure, and equality at 80 GB should be treated as invalid whenever total request weight is positive because it produces infinite pressure. Keep model objects themselves in output lists rather than converting them to copied records or indices.

active_paradigms.idea: Implement a dominance-pruned threshold branch-and-bound feasibility search with functools.lru_cache
active_paradigms.description: Exploit the exact threshold transformation already identified by the current code: for a proposed T, each GPU must satisfy sum_i (weight_i + T*size_i) <= 80*T, which also guarantees memory feasibility for positive weights. Rather than relying on a generic MILP at many thresholds, use a recursive branch-and-bound assignment search that places models in decreasing order of difficulty, such as descending size, transformed consumption, or the number of GPUs that can accept them. Represent each GPU by its remaining memory and remaining transformed threshold capacity, canonicalize the multiset of GPU states by sorting it, and memoize failed residual states with functools.lru_cache. At every recursion, skip symmetric choices that have identical residual state, try the tightest fitting GPU first, and prune if any remaining model fits nowhere. Add safe aggregate lower-bound pruning: the sum of remaining memory consumptions and transformed consumptions cannot exceed the sum of residual capacities, and each remaining item must fit individually in some bin. Use the greedy incumbent to establish an initial upper bound, then test a short deterministic sequence of lower-bound-centered thresholds; once a lower threshold is infeasible, do not revisit it. This directly addresses the current algorithm's weak local neighborhoods and the MILP time-limit sensitivity on small-to-medium hard cases, while preserving exact feasibility decisions for the tested bounds.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Find lower feasible maximum-KVPR thresholds exactly on instances small enough for search, with symmetry elimination aimed at difficult repeated-GPU states.
active_paradigms.cautions: Floating-point cache keys need deterministic rounding that is conservative: round residual capacities downward before claiming feasibility and avoid merging states that differ enough to alter fit decisions. Put a node/time cap around the recursion and immediately fall back to the current greedy/local-search placement if the cap is reached. Do not use an unsafe discretized DP that can accidentally accept over-memory placements; validate the final returned placement with original unrounded sizes.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use bounded exhaustive assignment search for small instances, with the exact KVPR as the objective
tried_paradigms.description: For small model counts, encode the entire placement as a point in a gpu_num-dimensional discrete grid per model and invoke brute force directly on that assignment space. The objective must compute model memory and request-weight totals from scratch, reject assignments exceeding 80 GB, and otherwise return the exact maximum KVPR; no surrogate or greedy ordering is needed. This provides a valuable exact method because the objective is non-additive: assigning one model changes both the numerator and denominator of a GPU's pressure, so local assignment costs are not reliable. It can beat the current program on the small and medium adversarial cases where its greedy construction is trapped and its move/swap neighborhood has no improving edge. Use a deterministic pre-check on the assignment-space size and invoke exhaustive search only below a strict threshold; otherwise retain the current greedy method as the fallback. Symmetry can be reduced in deterministic setup by fixing the first model to GPU zero, because GPU labels are interchangeable, which removes a factor of gpu_num without changing the optimum. Decode the best returned coordinate vector only after rechecking feasibility and preserve all models exactly once.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exact optimal maximum KVPR on small evaluator cases, improving the average score through guaranteed optimal solutions rather than heuristic local improvements.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The search space is gpu_num raised to the number of models, so it must be guarded aggressively to avoid evaluator timeouts. Invalid assignments need a finite high objective rather than exceptions, since the objective is called repeatedly. Do not use this unconditionally on large instances, and ensure the all-empty/zero-load pressure convention agrees with the evaluator's calculation.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a threshold-feasibility MILP with scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program uses decreasing single-model pressure greedy placement, followed by at most min(16,n) best-improving single moves or pair swaps. Its lexicographically sorted pressure objective is a useful tie-breaker, but it is still a shallow local search and can be trapped when improvement requires relocating several models together. Formulate the actual decision as binary assignment variables x[m,g], with every model assigned once and each GPU memory sum bounded by 80. For a fixed candidate maximum pressure T, feasibility is linear: on every GPU, sum((weight[m] + T * size[m]) * x[m,g]) must be at most 80*T. Use scipy.optimize.milp to solve this binary feasibility model, with a dense fixed grid of T values represented by threshold-selector binary variables in one MILP, or use a carefully bounded monotone threshold search if multiple calls are acceptable. Minimize the selected threshold rather than the current lexicographic surrogate, because the evaluator ultimately uses only each test case's maximum KVPR. A final placement is read directly from the integral assignment variables and therefore always respects memory constraints. This is especially promising when instances have enough models that multi-model exchanges dominate the quality gap.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Direct minimization of the per-test maximum KVPR, which improves the reciprocal mean score; assignment feasibility and 80 GB memory limits are enforced globally rather than repaired locally.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Do not use the nonlinear expression T multiplied by an unconstrained assignment sum directly in a basic MILP. Either solve linear fixed-T feasibility problems or use a finite threshold grid with proper big-M activation bounds. Set weights as req_rate/slo once, reject only genuinely infeasible instances, and use a sufficiently fine threshold grid so discretization does not erase the gain. Solver time must be capped; retain the current heuristic placement as a feasible incumbent/fallback if the MILP reaches its limit.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use exact subset-partition search over feasible GPU bundles via itertools.combinations
tried_paradigms.description: Exploit that the objective of a GPU depends only on the subset assigned to that GPU: its pressure is sum(weight)/ (80-sum(size)). For a candidate threshold T, enumerate model subsets that both fit in memory and satisfy their own pressure bound, then search for disjoint subsets covering all models using a bitmask partition recursion. The current greedy-plus-swap method cannot recognize a beneficial three-way or four-way rearrangement, whereas subset partitioning treats such coordinated exchanges as one decision. Generate candidate bundles with itertools.combinations, prune any subset whose memory exceeds 80 or whose pressure already exceeds T, and retain only nondominated bundles with respect to covered models and resource use. Branch on the uncovered model that has the fewest compatible bundles, which sharply reduces the partition search tree. Binary-searching or scanning candidate thresholds obtained from bundle pressures yields an exact optimum on small and medium instances. For larger instances, apply the same search only to the models on the highest-pressure GPUs after freezing clearly good bundles, making it a targeted exact large-neighborhood repair. This directly corrects the principal weakness of the incumbent: its 16 iterations and only one/two-model neighborhoods are arbitrary limits rather than consequences of the objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The maximum GPU KVPR through globally coordinated repartitioning, with particular emphasis on cases where the greedy seed requires multi-model cyclic exchanges.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This is exponential in the number of models, so use bitmasks only when model count is modest and impose a node/time budget. Memoize infeasible states by (remaining-model mask, GPUs-left), and symmetry-break equivalent GPUs by requiring a canonical first model in the next selected bundle. Empty GPUs are valid and have zero pressure. For large instances, use this as an exact repair on a restricted neighborhood and preserve the incumbent if the search budget is exhausted.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use randomized multi-start greedy construction with numpy.random.Generator.permutation and best incumbent selection
tried_paradigms.description: The incumbent's initial ordering is deterministic and based on each model's isolated pressure, so one unlucky early choice can consume the specific free memory needed by a later large model. Build many diversified constructions by using numpy.random.Generator.permutation to randomize within tiers of similar size, weight, or isolated pressure, while retaining descending order between clearly different tiers. In each construction, place a model into the feasible GPU that minimizes the resulting maximum pressure, not just that target GPU's pressure; break ties by preserving the largest useful free-memory capacity. Run the existing move-and-swap descent after each construction, but score the resulting complete placement strictly by max(load/free_memory), retaining the best incumbent across restarts. Add focused restarts that place largest models first, highest weights first, and highest weight-per-memory models first, because these orderings expose different packing failures. This is fundamentally different from exact optimization: it cheaply samples many basins of attraction and lets the already-working local improvement phase polish each one. It is likely to improve average evaluator score because the evaluator averages independent test-case maxima, so avoiding a few very poor greedy seeds matters more than tiny improvements on easy cases.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Robust reduction of worst-GPU KVPR across all generated cases, especially outlier instances where the deterministic greedy seed is trapped in a poor packing basin.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use a fixed seed for reproducibility and a bounded number of restarts to avoid evaluator timeout. Every randomized construction must still check remaining memory before assignment and must raise the same error only when no feasible placement exists. Compare placements using the actual scalar maximum pressure rather than only a lexicographic tuple, since the evaluator does not reward lower secondary pressures when the maximum is unchanged. Do not accept random worsening moves after local search; randomness should diversify starting packings, while incumbent replacement remains deterministic and monotone.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on capacity-safe GPU slots with exact marginal KVPR costs
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first uses a pressure-aware greedy assignment, then only accepts strictly lexicographically improving single moves or swaps; this is good at preserving feasibility but is easily trapped when several models must move simultaneously. Replace the initial greedy choice on small and medium instances with one global bipartite assignment call using scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Build a fixed number of capacity-safe slots per GPU, where a slot represents an allowed memory band and is only eligible for models whose size fits that band; reserve enough total slot memory so every returned assignment is memory-feasible. Set the cost of assigning model i to slot j on GPU g to the increase in a target pressure surrogate, using weight_i plus a congestion price proportional to size_i and the current planned residual-memory band. Add multiple slot types per GPU, including high-memory slots for large models and low-memory slots for high weight-per-size models, so the assignment can make coordinated exchanges that greedy moves cannot discover. The evaluator objective is the maximum KVPR, so costs should heavily penalize assignments that place high req_rate/slo models in the last residual-memory bands of a GPU. Keep the existing greedy placement only as a fallback if the slot construction cannot represent all models exactly. This differs from the failed MILP attempts because Hungarian assignment is a fast polynomial global matching method rather than branch-and-bound over binary placement variables.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the worst GPU KVPR by enabling coordinated global reassignment of models that are individually non-improving moves under the current greedy/local-search placement.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The slot design must guarantee that summed model_size on each GPU never exceeds 80 GB; do not merely use an average slot size. linear_sum_assignment requires a square or rectangular dense cost matrix and every model needs at least one finite-cost feasible slot. Use very large finite costs rather than infinity, validate the output memory exactly, and fall back to the proven greedy placement if slot feasibility is not guaranteed.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.algorithms.flow.min_cost_flow on a residual-memory state graph
tried_paradigms.description: The principal weakness of the current local search is that it explores only one move or one swap per iteration, whereas KVPR often improves only after a cycle involving three or more GPUs. Construct a single min-cost-flow graph in which each GPU is represented by discrete residual-memory states, for example integer or half-GB capacity layers, and each transition that consumes a model-sized amount of memory has a cost equal to the incremental increase of a convex pressure surrogate. Send one unit of flow for every model through an assignment layer into a GPU-state path, with model-specific edges allowed only when that model fits in the relevant capacity transition. Price the final low-residual states very sharply because the true denominator is 80 minus used memory; use the model weight req_rate/slo in the transition cost so high-request models avoid crowded GPUs. A single networkx.algorithms.flow.min_cost_flow call then finds a coordinated placement under the discretized capacity model, including reassignment cycles that the incumbent's move/swap neighborhood cannot reach. The returned GPU paths can be decoded directly into placement lists, and using conservative rounded-up model sizes ensures real memory feasibility. This is structurally unlike the failed configuration MILP: it exploits the one-dimensional 80-GB resource and a polynomial network-flow solver rather than enumerating configurations or invoking integer programming repeatedly.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Attack hard instances where memory fragmentation prevents beneficial multi-GPU exchanges, while directly preserving capacity and emphasizing the maximum-pressure bottleneck.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Capacity discretization must be conservative: round each model size upward and use a granularity that keeps the expanded graph small enough for evaluation time. The pressure objective is not exactly additive, so use increasing marginal costs calibrated to residual-memory bands and always calculate true KVPR after decoding. If an instance contains fractional sizes that make conservative discretization too wasteful, retain the current feasible incumbent rather than returning an infeasible flow-derived assignment.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.cluster.vq.kmeans2 to build balanced pressure-profile groups before direct placement
tried_paradigms.description: The existing ordering ranks models independently by their standalone pressure, which can mix large-memory models and high-request models in a way that creates denominator collapse on a few GPUs. Form a two-dimensional feature vector for every model using normalized model_size and normalized req_rate/slo, with the memory coordinate scaled strongly enough to reflect the nonlinear denominator risk. Call scipy.cluster.vq.kmeans2 with k equal to gpu_num to partition models into global pressure profiles, using deterministic initialization and a fixed seed for evaluator consistency. Interpret each centroid as a target GPU composition: groups with high total model size should receive relatively low total request weight, while high-weight groups should preserve more memory. Assign each cluster to one GPU and only use direct deterministic spill assignment for a cluster exceeding 80 GB, placing overflow into the cluster whose centroid and remaining capacity yield the lowest resulting true KVPR. This provides a fundamentally different basin of attraction from the incumbent greedy initialization, after which the existing move/swap cleanup can be retained if desired. It is especially useful when models naturally separate into memory-heavy/low-rate and light/high-rate populations, because good solutions deliberately counterbalance those populations rather than simply distributing standalone pressure ranks. The evaluator averages per-case maximum KVPR, so deterministic grouping avoids variance from randomized local-search restarts.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve initialization quality by balancing the joint size-versus-request composition on every GPU, reducing denominator collapse before local moves are considered.
tried_paradigms.cautions: kmeans2 does not itself enforce memory capacity or minimize the exact max-ratio objective, so it must not be trusted blindly as a final placement. Standardize features robustly and use deterministic initialization; otherwise one extreme req_rate/slo model can dominate all centroids. Validate every cluster's summed size, use the current greedy solution as a safe fallback, and do not return a cluster assignment unless every GPU satisfies the 80-GB limit.

tried_paradigms.description: The current program starts with pressure-aware greedy packing, performs at most 16 best single moves/swaps, and then optionally runs a short threshold MILP. Its greedy initialization is strong because it directly evaluates the post-placement KVPR, but the local search is myopic: accepting one best swap can block several compatible swaps whose combined effect is much better. Build an undirected graph whose vertices are currently placed models, with an edge only between models on different GPUs when swapping them is memory-feasible. Give each edge a conservative positive benefit based on the exact reduction in a lexicographic pressure vector, prioritizing reduction of the current maximum KVPR. Call max_weight_matching with maxcardinality=False to select a set of disjoint swaps that can be applied atomically. Before accepting the matching, compute all affected GPU loads and remaining memory jointly and compare the exact resulting maximum KVPR against the incumbent. Retain it only if every GPU remains within 80 GB and the exact objective strictly improves. This can escape the current one-swap-at-a-time basin while remaining deterministic and using the actual evaluator objective.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the worst-GPU KVPR after greedy construction, especially instances where several overloaded GPUs need coordinated exchanges rather than one individually improving move.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Edge benefits are not exactly additive because multiple swaps can affect the same GPU, so always validate the entire selected matching using recomputed loads and memory before committing. Use only strictly improving accepted states to prevent cycling. Limit candidate vertices to models on the most pressured GPUs plus plausible counterpart models, since a complete pair graph can be expensive.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment for a capacity-safe global slot reassignment
tried_paradigms.description: The present MILP is valuable on small n×gpu_num instances, but its repeated 0.15-second feasibility solves can return no useful incumbent on larger cases, leaving only the greedy/local solution. Construct one slot for every model currently on each GPU; a slot inherits the current model's memory size, so assigning a new model to a slot is allowed only when that model fits in that slot. Because the sum of slot capacities on every GPU equals its current total model memory, any complete allowed assignment automatically preserves the 80 GB memory bound. Define an assignment cost for model i into a slot of GPU g from a pressure-aware marginal score, for example the increase in squared excess above the incumbent maximum pressure using the GPU's current aggregate load and memory, with very large costs for non-fitting slots. Solve the one-to-one assignment globally with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment and rebuild each GPU from its assigned slots. Evaluate exact KVPR from the rebuilt placement and accept only a strict improvement. This is a globally coordinated reassignment rather than an exhaustive integer search or a continuous relaxation, and it can relocate many models in one call. Repeating is unnecessary; use it as a replacement neighborhood after the existing greedy placement or local moves.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Find multi-model global redistributions that lower the maximum KVPR while guaranteeing memory feasibility by construction.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The slot-capacity rule is deliberately conservative: a model fitting the total free capacity of a GPU but not an individual inherited slot is excluded. Costs are a surrogate, so exact post-solve validation is essential. Ensure every row has at least one finite cost; retaining its own slot guarantees this for a valid incumbent.

tried_paradigms.idea: Enumerate and evaluate feasible three-GPU relocation cycles with networkx.algorithms.cycles.simple_cycles
tried_paradigms.description: The current search considers only a single model move or a two-model swap, so it cannot perform a beneficial rotation where each destination needs a model to leave first before receiving another one. Make a directed candidate graph with one node per GPU, and add a directed edge source→target for a selected model when that model could be transferred after accounting for a bounded amount of anticipated outgoing memory from target. Restrict candidates to a few high-impact models per source, ranked by weight, size, or pressure contribution, so the graph remains small. Call networkx.algorithms.cycles.simple_cycles and inspect only cycles of length two or three. For each cycle, choose its edge-associated models and calculate the simultaneous change in load and memory on all involved GPUs exactly; this naturally handles moves that are infeasible in isolation but feasible as a rotation. Select the cycle that gives the greatest strict decrease in maximum KVPR and apply it atomically, optionally once after ordinary local search stalls. This directly targets a discrete structural blind spot of the incumbent rather than using another generic assignment optimizer.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape local optima caused by temporary memory infeasibility, with particular focus on cyclic exchanges among two or three nearly full GPUs.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A GPU-level cycle can have several candidate model choices, so store edge labels carefully and reject cycles that reuse a model or violate final memory. Do not enumerate all cycles in a dense full graph; cap candidate outgoing moves and cycle length at three. Score each candidate with exact final KVPR rather than summing per-edge improvements, since KVPR is nonlinear in aggregate memory and load.
